summary: A median age of 76.2 — one of the highest of any incorporated place in California — tells you almost everything about the rhythm of Desert Palms before you ever visit. Tucked into the eastern Coachella Valley's flat, sun-blasted floor with the Santa Rosa Mountains rising to the southwest, this 2.7-square-mile community runs on an average of 10.6 hours of daily sunshine and an annual high near 85°F, which in practice means summers routinely push well past 110°F while winters settle into the mild, dry warmth that draws seasonal residents. With only about 6,500 people and a density of roughly 2,400 per square mile, the streetscape is low-slung and quiet — golf-cart-friendly roads, minimal evening foot traffic, and almost no retail or dining corridors generating independent identity. A median home value of $526,500 against a median household income of around $82,000 produces a price-to-income ratio above 6:1, which is steep, though the $2,175 median rent suggests a parallel market of seasonal and part-time occupancy softening year-round demand. Nearly half of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, yet the local economy offers few major employers — healthcare systems and hospitality operations in neighboring Palm Desert and Indio absorb most working residents. Desert Palms is essentially a place optimized for stillness in a landscape that enforces it, where the tradeoff for cloudless skies and mountain-framed sunsets is a car-dependent insularity that makes even routine errands a regional affair.
